manifest: Bet C corpus manifest - native ~8 um human-labelled ink corpus (RESEARCH_PLAN_2026-27 s2 Bet C)
measured_from: live listings/headers on 2026-09-02 (dl.ash2txt.org, HF bucket API, S3 REST, GitHub API); labels and masks downloaded to the session scratchpad only (nothing vendored into the project); Aug-18 GROUND_TRUTH_AUDIT.json reused for the S3 PHerc0172 zarr shapes and the alignment proof

grand_totals.method_note: cm2 = pixel count x (pitch in cm)^2 on the label canvas; ink = label >= 128 (Scroll 1, antialiased) or > 0 (binary); surface = mask > 0; cross-check: sum of area_cm2.txt over 43 Scroll 1 segments = 2073.8 vs mask-derived 2052.8

sources.layout: 65-layer TIFF stack per segment (layers/00.tif..64.tif), uint16, uncompressed (compression=1), little-endian, IFD at end of file; canvas = flattened UV, same WxH as <seg>_mask.png; layer 32 = the segmented surface (VC convention); per-pixel geometry in <seg>.ppm; mesh <seg>.obj; area_cm2.txt + author.txt present
sources.label_format: all_labels/<seg>_inklabels.png (8-bit L, antialiased 0..255 for 41 files; binary 0/255 for 2; RGB for 2) + one .tiff; canvas = layers padded UP to the next multiple of 256 (GP prepare.py: pad = 256 - dim % 256, so an exact multiple gets +256); top-left aligned; threshold >= 128
sources.in_ink9um_training: partial: 4 labelled segments are ink_9um training segments (via the 2.4 um rescan pooled to 9.6 um, representations phercparis4-w01/w09/w03/w06 = 20230702185753/20230929220926/20231106155351/20231210121321); 8 more are superseded siblings of ink_9um segments (same segmentation lineage, overlapping surface); 32 are clean by segment id. NOTE the 7.91 um acquisition itself was never seen by ink_9um.

pool_to_9.36.z: legacy layers are 1 voxel = 7.91 um apart along the surface normal; 65 layers = 514 um. The ink_9um window is 21 slices x 9.36 um = 197 um = 24.9 legacy layers: take layers 20..44 (centre 32) and resample z by the same 1.1833 (or 25->21 slices). No integer z-pooling applies.
pool_to_9.36.alternative: train at native 7.91 (15.5% pitch mismatch to 9.36); ink_9um itself tolerates 9.596 vs 9.36 (2.5%) - prefer resampling so the comparison with ink_9um is clean

from_3.24.direction: downsample 2.889 (non-integer; e.g. 3x box mean then x0.963 resample, or one anti-aliased resample)
from_3.24.z: 65 x 3.24 um = 211 um deep -> 22.5 slices at 9.36 um: the whole stack becomes ~21-22 slices, i.e. it matches the 21-slice window with no z-crop; pool z by the same 2.889 (no integer pooling).

from_7.91.alternative: train at native 7.91 (15.5% pitch mismatch to 9.36); ink_9um itself tolerates 9.596 vs 9.36 (2.5%) - prefer resampling so the comparison with ink_9um is clean
from_7.91.availability: no released 7.91 um surface volume: to use it, map result.obj (3.24 frame) into the 7.91 volume with the affine in transforms/ (scale ~0.414 = 3.24/7.91) and re-render 21 x 9.36 um slices from the 7.91 zarr; the IR label transfers through the same UV canvas

ink9um_exclusion_and_dedup.purpose: dedup + hold-out bookkeeping for Bet C
ink9um_exclusion_and_dedup.physical_segment_key_rule: villa config keys physical segments as <scroll>:<w>; the 7.91 legacy stacks must be keyed to the SAME physical key when the segment id (or its superseded lineage, first 13 digits) matches an ink_9um paris4 row, so one physical surface gets one budget even if it has two representations (2.4-pooled and 7.91-native).
ink9um_exclusion_and_dedup.scroll1_unresolved: sheet-level overlap between the Sept-Dec 2023 GP-region segments (20231005123333/6, 20231022170900/1, 20231012173610, 20231012085431, 20231001164029, 20231004222109) and the 8 ink_9um paris4 wraps is NOT resolved (needs mesh intersection); May-Sept 2023 outer-wrap segments and recto/verso are the most independent
